mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A being the home side. Jointly examine: (a) Team A shots FOR all-prior vs recent-5, (b) Team A shots_on_target FOR all-prior vs recent-5, and (c) Team A goals FOR all-prior vs recent-5. The mechanism fires when shots volume is stable but shots_on_target and goals have diverged downward in the recent window relative to the long-run baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots_on_target FOR recent-5 falls below shots_on_target FOR all-prior while shots FOR remains stable, goals FOR recent-5 is suppressed relative to goals FOR all-prior — i.e., conversion efficiency declines non-proportionally with the on-target rate drop.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-goals conversion relationship: when Team A generates a high volume of shots (near its home average) but its recent shots-on-target rate has declined relative to its all-prior rate, its goals-for output is suppressed relative to its long-run average. The joint pattern of shots FOR, shots_on_target FOR, and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows captures a conversion-efficiency regime shift that is not visible from any single observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint three-observable relationship (shots, shots_on_target, goals) across two temporal windows simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to any single observable compared against a single band or baseline; the mechanism is about the cross-observable divergence pattern, not any one metric in isolation.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on Team A as home side. Jointly examine: Team A shots AGAINST, shots_on_target AGAINST, goals AGAINST, and fouls AGAINST across all-prior vs recent-5 windows. The mechanism is identified when shots/goals allowed rise while fouls allowed fall in the same recent window.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots AGAINST and goals AGAINST recent-5 are elevated above all-prior, but fouls AGAINST recent-5 is below all-prior, the defensive regime has shifted in a way that is not captured by any single observable — the combination of more shots allowed with fewer fouls suggests opponents are finding space without being fouled, a qualitatively distinct defensive state.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's defensive deterioration is asymmetric across observables: in the recent-5 window, shots conceded, shots_on_target conceded, and goals conceded have all risen sharply relative to all-prior averages, while fouls conceded has fallen. This joint pattern — more shots allowed but fewer fouls drawn — suggests a structural defensive-shape change rather than a simple form dip, and the cross-observable asymmetry (shots/goals up, fouls down) is the testable signal.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship across four distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals, fouls) in the AGAINST perspective, requiring simultaneous cross-observable comparison. No single-observable baseline or band captures the asymmetric directional divergence across these metrics.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on: (a) Team A corners FOR recent-5 vs all-prior (declining), and (b) Team B corners AGAINST recent-5 vs all-prior (rising sharply). The mechanism tests whether the cross-team joint signal — one team's recent attacking corner production declining while the opponent's recent defensive corner concession is rising — produces a non-additive interaction in expected corner volume.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B corners AGAINST recent-5 is substantially elevated above its all-prior average AND Team A corners FOR recent-5 is below its all-prior average, the two signals partially offset each other; the net corner volume relationship is non-linear relative to what either team's individual trend would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick concession rate has spiked sharply in recent matches relative to its all-prior average, while Team A's corner-kick production has declined in recent matches relative to its all-prior average. The joint cross-team divergence between Team B's corners AGAINST recent-5 and Team A's corners FOR recent-5 — both moving in the same direction (more corners for the attacking side) — creates a compounded corner-volume signal that neither team's individual trend alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct team-direction combinations of the same observable (Team A FOR recent vs all-prior, Team B AGAINST recent vs all-prior) and testing their joint interaction. This is not a single-observable single-band comparison; it is a cross-team, cross-window joint signal.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the second half as the within-match state. Jointly examine: (a) Team A goals FOR first-half vs second-half all-prior, and (b) Team B goals AGAINST first-half vs second-half all-prior. The mechanism fires when Team A's second-half scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate AND Team B's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half concession rate.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's goals FOR second-half all-prior exceeds goals FOR first-half all-prior, and Team B's goals AGAINST second-half all-prior exceeds goals AGAINST first-half all-prior, the second half is expected to be disproportionately goal-rich relative to the first half — a compounded within-match-state signal not reducible to either team's half-split in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Both teams show a within-match half-level asymmetry in goals: Team A scores more in the second half than the first half (all-prior), while Team B concedes more in the second half than the first half (all-prior). The joint alignment of Team A's second-half goal-scoring tendency with Team B's second-half goal-conceding tendency — both pointing in the same direction — is a cross-team, within-match-state interaction that is richer than either team's half-split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint cross-team within-match-state relationship: it requires simultaneously conditioning on the half (within-match state) and combining two distinct team-direction signals (Team A FOR, Team B AGAINST) for the same observable. Neither team's half-split alone, nor a simple home/away band, captures this joint alignment.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the second half as the within-match state. Jointly examine: (a) Team A cards_2h FOR and AGAINST vs competition context cards_2h, and (b) Team B cards_2h FOR and AGAINST vs competition context cards_2h. The mechanism tests whether both teams' second-half card rates sit on the same side of the competition norm (both elevated or both suppressed), producing a compounded signal.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team A's and Team B's second-half card rates (FOR and AGAINST) are jointly elevated above the competition-context second-half card baseline, second-half card volume rises with the joint elevation; when both are suppressed, it falls — the joint alignment amplifies the signal relative to either team's individual deviation from the norm.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards (cards_2h) environment is jointly shaped by both teams' second-half card tendencies relative to the competition context. Team A's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST (second-half) and Team B's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST (second-half) can be jointly compared against the competition-context cards_2h baseline to identify whether both teams simultaneously sit above or below the competition norm — a two-team, two-direction joint signal against a shared reference that is not reducible to either team's individual card rate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' second-half card rates (both FOR and AGAINST perspectives) against a shared competition-context reference, within the second-half state. It is not a single-observable single-band comparison; it is a four-signal joint alignment test against a competition baseline.
